summary: C30 adds one fixture-driven acceptance package that composes the existing domain boundaries into the complete local reference workflow: C08 enrollment with token-replay rejection, C09 mTLS batch ingest, C10/C11 signed applied configuration, C14/C15 bounded offline spool with explicit overflow loss, C16 duplicate acknowledgement, C17/C18 immutable segment projection and index, C19/C20 source-backed incident replay with durable idempotent triage, and a non-destructive C23 retention preview. The same accepted C05 store, C17/C18 segments and C24 certificate state back the real /readyz and the Sensors, Incidents and Certificates views; tests/browser/clone-to-value.spec.ts exercises them at 360px before and after a real restart. The harness writes outcome.json/runtime.json for the seed runner and fails explicitly for missing, unlicensed or malformed fixtures. A real staged-tree git clone runs npm run setup, Go vet and uncached race tests with the discovery guard (9 suites, 201 required anchors), the full workflow (8 passed steps, 6 passed typed negative cases, restore_equivalent true), seeded engine/storage/provider readiness across two server restarts with unchanged manifest and segment bytes, and the browser proof. npm run check passed 95 Node tests, npm run test:browser passed 21 Playwright tests, 6 Python tests and 338 checked JSON files/repository contracts passed, and go test -race ./... recorded 588 executed tests and 587 passes with the one opt-in C28 measurement skip. No product write ingress was added beyond the existing same-origin local triage. No commit, push, hosted Actions, published-artifact install, release or C40 claim.

npm run test:clone is the full clean-clone acceptance command. npm start alone reads explicitly configured local state and does not seed sensor state; the domain pages report unavailable until engine state options are supplied.
The test-only length-prefixed TLS batch envelope is not a published ingest protocol; the only browser write remains the same-origin local incident triage.

The recorded source identity covers the staged implementation/test/scenario tree before the progress, handoff, project-state and generated-web bookkeeping edits; no commit was created, so the final working-tree identity differs.
